p: from the side of the right,
and "negative commandment" from the side of the left,
from the side of the middle pillar.
And the Avos, Avraham and Yitzchak:
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (יְשַׁעְיָה מא, ח) אַבְרָהָם אֹהֲבִי,
as it is said (Yeshayahu 41:8), "Avraham who loved Me";
as they said in the Yerushalmi
"Know that you are one who loves,
and one who loves does not hate."
And alacrity pertains to positive commandments,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב (רַשִׁ״י לָרִי״ף עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה כ, ב).
as is written (Rashi on the Rif, Avodah Zarah 20b).
And this is what they said in the Gemara (Chullin 16a):
וּמִדַּת יִצְחָק פַּחַד יִצְחָק (בְּרֵאשִׁית לא, מב),
And Yitzchak's attribute is "the Fear of Yitzchak" (Bereishis 31:42),
"Know that you are one who fears,
and one who fears does not rebel."
וּמִדַּת זְהִירוּת, שֶׁהוּא בְּמִצְוֹת לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה,
And the attribute of carefulness pertains to negative commandments,
And all this stems from the attribute of Malchus,
"If I am a master, where is the fear of Me?"
and the servant is obligated to do his master's command
and not to do anything against his will.
And Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him —
כְּתִיב (מִיכָה ז, כ) תִּתֵּן אֱמֶת לְיַעֲקֹב;
it is written (Michah 7:20), "You will give truth to Yaakov";
and it is the Ilana d'Chayei, the Tree of Life,
and the letter vav, which is called "the sign of truth"
(זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג, רֵישׁ וַיִּקְרָא, ב, א).
And so it is written in the holy Zohar
"the Torah and the mitzvah, which are son and daughter."
the Torah is likened to light and a mitzvah to a lamp:
"Just as a lamp gives light only for a time,
so a mitzvah gives light only for a time;
and just as light shines forever,
and Yitzchak Avinu, peace be upon them,
since their portion is the positive commandments
which give light only for a time;
for whoever is of his seed
לֹא יוּכַל לַעֲקוֹר שֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל מִמֶּנּוּ,
cannot uproot the name "Yisrael" from himself,
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁחָטָא יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא.
"Even though he sinned, he is still a Yisrael."
And he merited to be a chariot for the Name Havayah.
"The lip of truth shall be established forever";
and it includes the holiness of Avraham and Yitzchak,
And this is the significance of the festival of Sukkos,
which corresponds to Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him:
it is a mitzvah that one fulfills
And although there is the mitzvah of Shabbos,
which also lasts the entire day,
אֲבָל אֵינוֹ רַק יוֹם אֶחָד מֵעֵת לְעֵת,
it is only one day, a single twenty-four hours;
nor is it by active doing,
only by guarding — by sitting back and refraining.
כֵּיוָן שֶׁהוּא רָגִיל בִּמְלָאכָה כָּל הַשָּׁבוּעַ
since he is used to working all week
it is like one to whom a sin came
and who was saved from it,
as though he did a mitzvah,
lasts seven full days around the clock,
and it is a positive commandment, performed by active doing.
And although it would seem that all seven days
מְקַיֵּים הַמִּצְוָה רַק בְּשֵׁב וְאַל תַּעֲשֶׂה,
one fulfills the mitzvah only passively,
but it is brought in the Gemara (Sukkah 2a):
בַּסֻּכּוֹת תֵּשְׁבוּ שִׁבְעַת יָמִים (וַיִּקְרָא כג, מב) —
"'You shall dwell in sukkos seven days' (Vayikra 23:42):
the Torah said, all seven days
and dwell in a temporary dwelling."
Now this is difficult: it is superfluous
for it to say "all seven days,"
since it already said "you shall dwell seven days";
גַּם מַה שֶּׁאָמַר צֵא מִדִּירַת קֶבַע
"The Torah said, dwell in a temporary dwelling,
is that the mitzvah of sukkah all seven days
means that at every single moment
one must be moving from level to level,
וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בַּגְּמָרָא (מוֹעֵד קָטָן ט, ב):
This is along the lines of what they said in the Gemara (Moed Katan 9b):
"May your house be destroyed and your lodging be settled" —
for this world is your lodging, etc.
It is as if he leaves his house
and so he fulfills a positive commandment actively,
and passively in that he does not go out.
And the festival of Sukkos is
from the side of the middle pillar:
until one then merits, on Shemini,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (תִּקּוּנֵי זֹהַר תִּקּוּן יג, כט, ב),
as has been explained many times.
For this reason the mitzvah of sukkah
is mentioned in connection with Yaakov,
and as they said in the holy Zohar
(חֵלֶק א קעב, ב; וְחֵלֶק ג ק, ב);
and in Tishrei they will be redeemed (Rosh Hashanah 11b);
and this is "The lip of truth shall be established forever."
it is brought that a lamp is
only wick and oil without light,
while "Torah is light" is the flame.
And we have said that in every mitzvah
which is the intent of the mitzvah —
to fulfill the command of the Creator —
and the holiness from the mitzvah,
for which we recite the blessing
"Who has sanctified us with His commandments and commanded us":
that shines only for a time.
וְתוֹרָה בְּעַצְמוֹ גַּם כֵּן מִצְוַת עֲשֵׂה
And Torah itself is also a positive commandment,
like all the two hundred forty-eight positive commandments,
וְהוּא רַק נֵר וּפְתִילָה בְּלֹא אוֹר;
and as such it is only a lamp and wick without light;
and the intent of the positive commandment of Torah study
And the difference is that the light of a mitzvah —
the Torah that comes from the mitzvah —
וְהַתּוֹרָה אוֹר מִמִּצְוַת עֲשֵׂה שֶׁל תּוֹרָה
while the Torah light from the positive commandment of Torah study
as has been explained many times.
